title: Toasted Oat and Brown Butter Buttermilk Pancakes
changes_from_base: Toasted steel-cut oats are blended to a powder and mixed with the flour, and the butter is browned before it goes in; no soured cream is used.
summary: Hearty oat pancakes with the nutty depth of browned butter and buttermilk tang, crispy-edged and satisfying.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast oats
steps.text: Toast 170 g steel-cut oats in a dry medium frying pan over medium heat, stirring often, until nutty (about 4 min); tip into a bowl to cool slightly.

steps.title: Brown butter
steps.text: Melt 57 g unsalted butter in the same pan over low heat, swirling, until the solids are golden brown and it smells nutty (about 2 min); pour into a large bowl.

steps.title: Grind and mix
steps.text: Blend the cooled oats to a fine powder on high (about 1 min); return to the bowl and whisk in 140 g plain flour, 2 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda, ½ tsp fine salt and 35 g caster sugar.

steps.title: Whisk wet
steps.text: Heat a griddle over medium heat and rub it with kitchen paper dipped in oil. Whisk 2 large eggs and 450 ml buttermilk into the brown butter, add the dry mix and whisk until no dry streaks remain but the batter is still lumpy.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Ladle 80 ml portions and spread to 10 cm rounds; cook undisturbed until bubbles form on top and the base is deep golden, then flip and cook until golden.

steps.title: Keep warm
steps.text: Keep warm on a wire rack in a warm oven while you cook the rest; serve straight away with warm maple syrup.

tips: Toasting the oats before grinding them brings out their nuttiness, a flavour amplified by the browned butter.
Grind the oats to a fine powder so they disappear into the batter; coarser pieces can make the pancakes gritty.
Leave the pancakes undisturbed on the griddle until bubbles cover the surface—this gives them a deep golden base and helps them cook through evenly.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
